findings.title: Pause action is never rendered for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
findings.body: The new list view supplies only a promRule and no rulerRule, and this PR computes canPause from the new Grafana prom abilities. Rendering still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule), which is false when rulerRule is undefined, and MenuItemPauseRule also requires that ruler rule. Consequently Pause never appears in the new rule list even for editable, unpaused Grafana rules, despite the newly added ability check.

findings.title: Delete action is never rendered for Prometheus-only Grafana rules
findings.body: canDelete can now become true through useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities when only a promRule is available, but the Delete menu item is additionally gated by `rulerRule &&` and its handler is typed to require a RulerRuleDTO. In the new GrafanaGroupLoader/FilterView list, rulerRule is always undefined, so users with delete permission cannot delete a rule from the list. The GrafanaGroupLoader test even encodes this by expecting only four menu items despite granting delete permission.

findings.title: Silence action opens no drawer for Prometheus-only rules
findings.body: In the new list view RuleActionsButtons receives only promRule, so `rule` is undefined. Clicking Silence in AlertRuleMenu sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but this line only mounts SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. The click therefore has no visible effect and silencing from the alert list is broken, even though the new prom abilities may show the Silence menu item.

findings.title: skipToken does not actually skip Grafana prom abilities
findings.body: Callers pass skipToken for cloud rules, non-Grafana prom rules, or absent prom rules, but useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities converts it to undefined and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities still computes real abilities. For an undefined rule, Duplicate becomes [AlwaysSupported, Grafana-rule-create permission] because provisioned/plugin checks are false and loading is false. AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler result, so Duplicate can appear for cloud or ruler-only rules based solely on an unrelated Grafana create permission. A skipped rule should return [false, false] for every action.

findings.title: Federated rule groups lose their immutable status
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously derived isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) for CombinedRules and marked federated rules unsupported for Update/Delete. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which discards the group and hardcodes isFederated to false. Federated Mimir rule groups in existing CombinedRule consumers will therefore be offered edit/delete actions that federated groups do not support.

findings.title: Grafana recording rules can no longer be paused
findings.body: The ruler-based ability used isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which is true for both Grafana alerting and recording rules, for Pause/Restore. The new prom-based ability uses isAlertingRule instead, so Pause and Restore are unsupported for Grafana recording rules. Since the list view no longer supplies a ruler rule to provide the old ability, recording rules lose pause/unpause entirely.

findings.title: Grafana rule list items are rendered without a React key
findings.body: The switch previously rendered GrafanaRuleLoader with key={key}; the replacement GrafanaRuleListItem omits the key while the datasource and unknown branches keep theirs. In this dynamically appended/filtered list, index-based reconciliation can reuse the wrong component instance and its local state such as modals, drawers, and menus, in addition to producing React key warnings. Restore key={key} on GrafanaRuleListItem.
